limitations: No database connection was made; DATABASE_URL/Postgres/Supabase were not contacted, and drizzle-kit was not executed. All schema and migration claims are from static repository files only.
electron/main.ts and electron/preload.ts were only grep-scanned for a local-database dependency (better-sqlite3), not fully read for other local persistence paths.

External LLM provider calls in src/lib/ai/llm-client.ts (OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini) are outbound API contracts to third-party services, not this project's own persisted/shared state, and were out of scope for this pass beyond noting their presence.

jCodeMunch reference/importer tools were not used for this run because the claims below (no fetch call to /api/projects anywhere in src/, no route for /api/projects in api/index.ts) were established directly by reading the relevant files and by a repository-wide grep, which is a stronger channel than the index for confirming an absence.

findings.title: Postgres projects/clientProfiles tables are unreachable in production: the Vercel serverless entry never routes /api/projects

identity.assertion: The production Vercel serverless handler (api/index.ts, the only file under api/, targeted by vercel.json's rewrite of /api/(.*) to /api) only implements routing for pathname === '/api/health' and pathname.startsWith('/api/auth/'); any other path (including /api/projects) falls through to the 404 branch. The /api/projects GET and POST routes exist only in server/src/index.ts, a separate Hono app started by the 'server:dev' npm script (tsx server/src/index.ts), which is not deployed by vercel.json and is not referenced anywhere by api/index.ts.

evidence.detail: Main Handler switches only on '/api/health' and startsWith('/api/auth/'); default branch returns 404 { error: 'Not found', path: pathname }. No import of server/src/index.ts or its projects routes.
rewrites: '/api/(.*)' -> '/api' (i.e. api/index.ts is the sole serverless function for all /api/* traffic in production).

app.get('/api/projects', ...) and app.post('/api/projects', ...) are defined only in this file's standalone Hono app, which is started via serve() only 'if (!process.env.VERCEL)' (line 71) — i.e. never in the Vercel deployment.

scripts.server:dev = 'tsx server/src/index.ts' is the only way this Hono app (and its /api/projects routes) runs; there is no build/deploy script that bundles server/src/index.ts into the Vercel function.

verification.note: Independently confirmed alongside architecture-001/stack-001: api/index.ts (sole Vercel production entry per vercel.json) does not implement /api/projects; server/src/index.ts, which does, is never deployed there.

findings.title: Client's real project data model (MarlexProject, localStorage) has no field overlap with the Postgres projects table it nominally mirrors

identity.assertion: MarlexProject (src/types/index.ts, the type actually used app-wide via the zustand store in src/lib/store/useMarlexStore.ts) has fields id, name, brandHandle, authorName, bgColor, accentColor, textColor, font, photoOpacity, members, createdAt, updatedAt. The Postgres `projects` table (server/src/db/schema.ts) has an entirely different, non-overlapping shape: id, userId, clientProfileId, title, rawInput, slidesJson, telegramPost, linkedInPost, threadsJson, status, createdAt, updatedAt. No route in the codebase converts between the two shapes.

evidence.detail: export interface MarlexProject { id; name; brandHandle; authorName; bgColor; accentColor; textColor; font; photoOpacity; members; createdAt; updatedAt }
export const projects = pgTable('projects', { id, userId, clientProfileId, title, rawInput, slidesJson, telegramPost, linkedInPost, threadsJson, status, createdAt, updatedAt })

persist(...) middleware config name: 'marlex-content-storage-v5' — this is the actual runtime store for MarlexProject[]; a repo-wide search for 'api/projects' or 'fetch(' targeting the API found zero call sites in src/.

FAQ copy states (Russian): carousel data and history are stored locally on the user's computer and are not sent to or saved on third-party servers — consistent with the store using only localStorage persistence, not the /api/projects endpoints.

findings.title: /api/projects has no auth check: GET returns all users' projects unfiltered, POST inserts rows with no userId and no session validation

identity.assertion: app.get('/api/projects') runs `db.select().from(projects)` with no WHERE clause and no session/auth check, returning every row in the table to any caller. app.post('/api/projects') builds `newProject` without ever reading the caller's session or setting `userId` (the projects.userId column, a FK to user.id, is simply omitted), and performs no better-auth session check before inserting.

evidence.detail: app.get('/api/projects', async (c) => { const allProjects = await db.select().from(projects); return c.json({ success: true, data: allProjects }); }) — no auth.api.getSession() call, no eq(projects.userId, ...) filter.

app.post('/api/projects', ...) builds newProject = { id, title, rawInput, slidesJson, telegramPost, linkedInPost, threadsJson, status, createdAt, updatedAt } — userId is never assigned, so every insert leaves projects.userId NULL despite the column existing specifically to scope ownership.
projects.userId is nullable (references user.id, onDelete 'set null'), which is what allows the POST handler's omission to silently succeed instead of failing at the DB layer.

verification.note: Independently verified: server/src/index.ts (the only file implementing /api/projects) is gated by `if (!process.env.VERCEL)` and started only via `npm run server:dev`; the deployed Vercel production entry (api/index.ts, sole target of vercel.json's /api/(.*) rewrite) does not implement /api/projects at all. No importer, CI step, or deploy config runs server/src/index.ts anywhere besides local development. The code-level vulnerability (no session check, no userId scoping) is confirmed as written; it is not reachable on the public production deployment today.

findings.title: No Drizzle migrations exist or are tracked in git despite drizzle.config.ts targeting a migrations directory

identity.assertion: drizzle.config.ts declares out: './drizzle' as the migrations directory, but no './drizzle' directory exists in the working tree and git log for 'drizzle/' returns no commits. package.json has no db:generate/db:push/db:migrate script wiring drizzle-kit (a devDependency) into any workflow, so schema changes to server/src/db/schema.ts have no versioned, reviewable, or rollback-capable migration path recorded in the repo.

evidence.detail: defineConfig({ schema: './server/src/db/schema.ts', out: './drizzle', dialect: 'postgresql', dbCredentials: { url: process.env.DATABASE_URL! } })

scripts block contains only dev, build, dev:electron, build:electron, server:dev — no drizzle-kit generate/push/migrate script; drizzle-kit ^0.30.4 is present only as a devDependency with no invocation site found in the repo.

findings.title: Auth/schema definitions are hand-duplicated between server/src/db/schema.ts and api/index.ts with no shared source

identity.assertion: api/index.ts re-declares the user/session/account/verification/projects pgTable definitions inline (rather than importing server/src/db/schema.ts), per commit 9ffd501c ('Make Vercel API directory completely self-contained with internal schema, db and auth'). The two copies already differ in the auth config that consumes them: api/index.ts's betterAuth() adds 'file://' and '*' to trustedOrigins and sets advanced.defaultCookieAttributes (sameSite: 'none', secure: true), neither of which exist in server/src/auth.ts. A schema.ts change (e.g. adding a column) will not propagate to api/index.ts unless someone manually edits both files.
identity.symbol: projects, user, session, account, verification (duplicated pgTable declarations)

evidence.detail: Inline pgTable('user'/'session'/'account'/'verification'/'projects', ...) definitions duplicate server/src/db/schema.ts field-for-field at the time of this audit, but are maintained as a separate, unimported copy.
Canonical schema used by drizzle.config.ts and by server/src/db/index.ts's `drizzle(client, { schema })`.

betterAuth({ ... trustedOrigins: [..., 'file://', '*'], advanced: { defaultCookieAttributes: { sameSite: 'none', secure: true } } }) differs from server/src/auth.ts's betterAuth({ ... trustedOrigins: [...] }) which has neither 'file://'/'*' nor an `advanced` block — direct evidence the two copies have already drifted.

findings.title: POST /api/projects always INSERTs, so its documented 'create or update' behavior fails with a primary-key violation on repeat calls with the same id

identity.assertion: The route comment 'Database API: Create or update project' implies upsert semantics, but the handler unconditionally calls `db.insert(projects).values(newProject)` with no onConflictDoUpdate and no prior existence check. projects.id is a non-generated text primaryKey, so re-POSTing the same body.id (the natural way a client would 'update' a project it already created) throws a unique-constraint violation caught only by the generic catch block, returning a 500 rather than performing an update.

evidence.detail: // Database API: Create or update project

await db.insert(projects).values(newProject); — no .onConflictDoUpdate(...), no SELECT-then-branch logic; id is taken directly from body.id (line 48: `id: body.id || 'proj_' + Date.now()`) with no server-side existence check.
projects.id = text('id').primaryKey() — client-supplied, not DB-generated, so a repeated id from the same client is exactly the case an 'update' would hit.
